teacher_info.introduction:
After receiving a Masters of Teaching in 2010 and TEFL certification in 2015, I have been teaching English as a second language to foreign language learners at a large language school. I've had the opportunity to teach hundreds of students from a variety of countries, ranging from beginners to advanced/fluent. I have taught group lessons and private lessons. I specialize in private lessons and have multiple repeat students who I have been teaching for years now. They are on the path to complete fluency, which is something I am proud of. 

My classes focus on vocabulary, grammar, and pronunciation (accent reduction). I teach structured lessons with topics such as business, travel, conversation, and other necessities. Additionally, I love unstructured, casual lessons (if that is what you want), but understand the importance of structured classes. 

Teaching online has shown me that students learn in a variety of ways, some being more effective than others. After each lesson, I provide feedback on what students have done well and the steps they can take to improve their skills. 

One of my other responsibilities is as an academic writing skills tutor for two large universities, where I help students develop their academic English skills and fix grammar, sentence structure, and spelling issues. I do these corrections in British English and American English, depending on the student's preferred writing style. 

Finally, I spend most of my time abroad and am therefore familiar with the difficulties of communicating in a foreign language when you have not developed the necessary skills to communicate clearly and effectively. I am here to help you improve your communication skills so you can avoid the problems and awkward situations I have when doing business, traveling, or any other activity using a foreign language. Best wishes!

pro_course_detail.title: English for Daily Life - Practical English
pro_course_detail.description:
“English for Daily Life” is about the vocabulary necessary in order to live in a foreign country, so the class is perfect for people who live in a foreign country or who are planning to move. I have lived in three different countries, so I know you will definitely need to be familiar with these topics.

We learn things like:
* Going to the doctor
* Calling the police
* Calling an ambulance
* Going to the dentist
* Going to the post office
* Going to the vet
* Buying something at the grocery store
* Calling the government
* Calling the immigration department
* Filling out forms and paperwork
* Insurance vocabulary
* Rental contracts
* Sending a letter
* Introducing yourself to your neighbors
* Many more!

Before class I will send you a list of topics and you can choose the ones you want to learn. I will send topic-related vocabulary and we will practice the vocabulary and dialogues during class together.  

If you want a class similar to those you took in school (with a focus on vocabulary, grammar, pronunciation, and other skills) please schedule GENERAL ENGLISH. In General English classes, we learn topics like describing food, talking about hobbies, going on vacation, etc. "English for Daily Life" is about living and communicating when you live abroad.

pro_course_detail.description:
All components of general English (speaking, listening, writing, grammar, and vocabulary) are in this course! General English lessons are traditional and have structured activities. In each class, we:
1. Learn grammar rules, vocabulary, pronunciation, and listening. 
2. Do activities to practice what we've learned. (Fill in the blank, complete the sentence, match the dialogue with a response, put vocabulary in a category, etc.)
3. Do a role play or have a conversation to use what we learned earlier and speak naturally.

Lessons teach all aspects of language, including grammar, pronunciation, vocabulary, conversational English, reading, and writing skills. 

We use the following materials:
* Textbooks (I have textbooks or the student can bring their own)

Writing practice is typically assigned as homework and is checked during class. We will look at essay structure, transitioning, paragraphs, and vocabulary. There is an offline writing service available too. See below for information.

Need an effective teacher who easily explains step by step?

This is a chance to practice your English skills, for me to assess your level, and for you to get an idea of my teaching style. 

You must be at least 6.5 years old for my class. For young beginners, we will introduce each other first, and l will teach you some common etiquette when meeting someone. Then I will show you some pictures where I will ask you some questions about them. I will also teach you  how to ask for help when you don' understand a word or don't have an answer. Next you will read  a short picture story with more question and answer time. Here I will get an an idea of your grammar experience and comprehension level. After that, we will play a learning game for you to learn some new vocabulary and demonstrate more speaking. Last, I will review the 44 sounds of the English language to see what sounds you are having trouble pronouncing. At the end, parents and I can meet to talk about strengths, weaknesses, and the best learning plan as well as further discounts.

If you are older we can talk and learn about anything you want or I will choose the topics.

Whether you are  a young or an adult, I will correct and explain all errors both verbally and in writing.

pro_course_detail.description:
Create an informal but very useful outline for any writing project in English: emails,  essays, articles, speeches, work memos and more . A good outline helps you remember all the thoughts you want to write. This is especially true when you write in English which has such a huge vocabulary.

And no one is going to see your outline except you.  So, you don't have to be neat, put it onto a specific format, or concentrate on spelling or grammar.  An outline will benefit you no matter what your English level -  from intermediate to proficient.

In this class you'll learn:
*How to get over the dread of doing an outline.
* Why an outline works a lot better then memorizing ideas and details.
*The difference between a informal and academic outline.
* The wonderful fact that you don't have to follow your outline to successfully write. You can change your mind about what to write - or you can change your outline.

We'll start right away on your outline.  First you'll pick your writing topic.  Next, you'll write down your thoughts about what you want to communicate in your writing.  If you can't think of anything to write about, I'll interview you to find out your interests.  We'll then turn your outline into to a real piece of writing that you can use.

Class Expectations:

pro_course_detail.title: Pronunciation & Accent Practice 🎤
pro_course_detail.description:
Talk like an American! Whether you want to improve your ability to communicate clearly with native speakers, imitate your favorite American TV stars, or sound more natural in your everyday speech—great accent ability begins with learning to listen, to hear the subtle differences between sounds and learn to mimic them yourself. In this class, we focus on three main areas of accent training:

(1) Pronunciation, particularly English short vowels and difficult consonants,
(2) Intonation, or the "music" of the language,
(3) Connected speech, or how to link and blend words naturally like an American English speaker,
(4) Common native expressions and filler words.

To begin, I'll analyze your current speech level and identify target areas to strengthen your pronunciation. At the sentence level, we'll look at how the English language stresses its words, and discuss the difference between stress-timed and syllable-timed resources. We'll also identify patterns in the ways that native English speakers blend their words when speaking casually (which should help you better understand TV shows and movies!) To round it all out, we'll practice including some common expressions and filler language in your speech, especially while speaking casually.

Lessons are tailored to each individual student. I draw upon a variety of resources to help to develop your speech skills, and will include sound clips for you to practice what we learn in each session. You can do it—let's have fun with accents!

pro_course_detail.title: English Writing & Grammar 📝
pro_course_detail.description:
In this class, we focus on improving grammar and writing in the English language. Phrasal verbs, past perfect verb tenses, zero conditionals, and more! We will use short and long writing exercises (depending on the student's goals and preferences) to practice the grammar you're studying. As a writer, I love playing with words, finding the best way to express an idea, and I want to convey that grammatical enthusiasm over to you! 🤓📝

Short exercise: Compose a series of sentences using the target grammar in our lesson (for example, one sentence for each of the twelve English verb tenses). Then in class, we'll review the nuances and differences in meaning, both implied and explicit, by tweaking the words.

Long exercise: Write a short paragraph (100-500 words) telling me about a day in your life, a short story or essay, or an opinion of a book or TV show that you've recently watched. Anything that interests you! Then, during class, we will review your writing and correct it for grammar, language use, clarity, and word choice. We will discuss the differences in professional versus casual tone. This is a good class for students wanting to improve their essay-writing, professionals wanting to improve their email communications, and all other writers wanting to improve their command of English.

pro_course_detail.title: Business English 💼
pro_course_detail.description: In this class, we'll review the ways that English in the workplace can differ from friendly conversational English between friends; business English often uses a different set of vocabulary terms, idioms, and higher register of formality and politeness. We'll explore different ways to write an email, have conversations with your boss, and talk in meetings, with a bit of situational role play for you to practice! I draw upon my own experience working professionally as an architect, and I also encourage students to bring in examples of real-life language they encounter at their job, so we can discuss situations specific to their jobs and careers. teacher_info.teaching_style: The first session with me is typically free of lesson plans and study points. No matter the student's level of English, it's important to establish a fluid communication as a basis for the future of our classes. While we get to know each other, I am quietly taking notes on the student's habits in speaking English as well as their areas of interest to use as a focus for lesson plans. We will exercise all four areas of language: speaking, reading, writing and listening, but always with a heavier focus on speaking. As the classes progress we rotate through these areas while constantly adding vocabulary and grammar rules, as I help the student to fix their habits from the root of the mistakes.
